1) Gaming.
2) Upgradability.
3) Raw Processing Power.
4) Modularity.

A laptop is adequate if you only need no more than 2 of the above. I use the right tool for the job, and the demands of what I need to accomplish require top of the line hardware performance.

The benefit of using cutting-edge hardware is you do not get stuck in the 2-3 year upgrade cycles. Every 5-7 years I can spend a few grand for completely top of the line hardware and it will easily last 5-7 years, where the laptop would be lucky to make it half that long due to the natural self-cannibalization of form factor and heat eating electronics. My last desktop computer was an i7-980X base and is being retired for a i7-6950X 7+ years later. Can't ask for a better "bang for your buck" when the only change since I bought the previous system was a graphics card upgrade every 3 years, which is just a utility/luxury upgrade so I can still enjoy gaming on the side and is not even necessary for the core functionality of the system.

My build PC is now 7 or 8 years old. Only the occasional new hard drive there is nothing wrong with it. it still does everything i need to do and some. No plan on upgrading for a while yet. And when i do upgrade i do the same as you, buy top of the line and i will be set for another 8 or so years.
